gen-gf-gveret-levin-general-sans: Gveret Levin brings an inviting, hand-drawn feel, with rope-bodied curves and a pronounced x-height. General Sans keeps its pressure steady and its bends smooth, so text runs on easily, though a line or two is ideal.
gen-gf-gveret-levin-manrope: Rope-heavy curves and a hand-drawn feel give Gveret Levin its friendly look, with a pronounced x-height. Manrope keeps every curve mouth bright and open on a single line width, ideal for a line or two.
gen-gf-gveret-levin-montserrat: Gveret Levin is friendly and hand-drawn, its rope-bodied curves sitting on a pronounced x-height. Yet Montserrat, the sans-serif below, opens oversized e and a counters wide, though it's best taken in bites rather than pages.
gen-gf-gveret-levin-satoshi: Gveret Levin looks hand-drawn and inviting, its curves carrying a rope's heft with a pronounced x-height. Satoshi stands out for its soaring x-height and an e never squeezed shut, best enjoyed in brief glances.
gen-gf-gveret-levin-switzer: Rope-bodied curves give Gveret Levin its friendly, hand-drawn character, topped by a pronounced x-height. And Switzer, the sans-serif here, keeps c tips apart in wire-like letterforms, reading cleanly for a couple of lines.
gen-gf-hachi-maru-pop-fs-amulya: Relaxed, stretched-out letter spacing gives Hachi Maru Pop a hand-drawn ease, with diagonals matching its stems. But Amulya feels contemporary beside it, with generous gaps in its curves, though long paragraphs aren't what this pair does.
gen-gf-hachi-maru-pop-fs-recia: Marker-drawn plainness, that's Hachi Maru Pop, with stretched-out spacing and a relaxed hand. Yet Recia, a serif with medium contrast and sharp authority, steps in underneath, ready for brief stretches.
gen-gf-hachi-maru-pop-fs-synonym: Relaxed and inviting, Hachi Maru Pop spaces its hand-drawn letters wide, with an e eye opening clearly right. Yet Synonym, drawn in constant ink with generous curve openings, supplies the steadiness, best kept to a couple of lines.
